rationale: The plan correctly diagnoses the n=1-per-group design, refuses any Wald/LRT p-value or FDR for genes, delivers normalized counts plus descriptive log2 fold changes, and names a replicated design (>=2-3 per group) as what would be needed for inference — all matching the reference. QC (library sizes, blind VST, PCA, distance heatmap) is present with an honest statement of what two samples can and cannot reveal, the >=10-counts-in->=1-sample filter is minimal and justified, and median-of-ratios size factors are computed inside DESeq2 with no pre-scaling. Two technical problems: apeglm shrinkage requires a dispersion estimate, and with zero residual degrees of freedom DESeq2 cannot estimate within-group dispersion, so the 'shrunken' LFC step is not actually feasible or meaningful here; the plan asserts it without acknowledging that dependency. The fgsea layer then reintroduces inference through the back door — BH-adjusted enrichment p-values and a padj<0.05 'significant set' call built on a ranking derived from a single pairwise ratio, which carries no replication-based error control despite the exploratory framing. Reporting is otherwise thorough and appropriately caveated.
